title: Define compat/verify story against runtime version ranges
Hermes plugin packaging + distribution scoping (marketplace readiness)
description:
## Motivation

The agentguides launch plan (/Users/brian/workspace/github/agentguides/infra/.plans/launch-plan-2026-06-20.md, line 336) calls Hermes marketplace inclusion "the single highest-leverage distribution decision", and its Open scoping items list (line 459) says "Hermes plugin packaging mechanics — need a separate scoping doc". That doc was never written. This epic is the scoping/mechanics work that the ag-infra-cdp bead ("Package + submit Hermes plugin", P1, agentguides/infra hive) depends on; ag-infra-cdp stays in its own hive and is referenced here only.

Known blockers recorded runtime-side:
- Hermes ACP/MCP environment-backend filesystem view (M6): the hermes-spawned guide MCP process cannot stat host guide paths (ENOENT in a different mount namespace). See /Users/brian/workspace/github/agentguides/runtime/.planning/research/hermes-acp-mcp-tools-blocked.md. The "0 tools" half is FIXED (HERMES_HOME forward); guide-root resolution remains OPEN.
- Binary-distribution stub: /Users/brian/workspace/github/agentguides/runtime/src/agentguides/harness/hermes.py (~line 735) ships two install models — Model B "shim" (guide already on PATH) works; Model A "binary" (plugin installs the binary) is a v0.5.4 STUB that hard-exits, gated on an agentguides.io signed-release endpoint.

## Proposed approach

1. Author the packaging-mechanics scoping doc covering: bundle format (what `hermes plugins install agentguides/hermes-plugin` actually ships — git-managed tree + `.local/` operator state per README), versioning (plugin.yaml/pyproject both at 0.1.0; how plugin version relates to runtime `agentguides` version), sync/cron behavior on install (cron/guide-sync.json symlink into $HERMES_HOME/cron/), and profile.toml defaults (policy=all, empty include list; per src/guide_plugin/profile_config.py).
2. Decide the install model: commit to shim (Model B) for marketplace v1 and explicitly defer Model A, or scope the signed-release fetch. Route around the stub rather than blocking on agentguides.io releases.
3. Define the Hermes marketplace submission checklist (manifest requirements, listing metadata, install/uninstall verification, default vs community listing per launch plan line 336).
4. Define a compat/verify story: which runtime version ranges the plugin supports, how install-time detection (`guide --version` in the shim hook) enforces it, and a repeatable verification matrix.

## Scope / non-goals

In scope: scoping doc, install-model decision, submission checklist, compat/verify definition, contingency plans for the M6 blocker.
Non-goals: the actual marketplace submission (that is ag-infra-cdp in agentguides/infra); fixing the upstream M6 environment-backend issue in hermes itself; implementing the agentguides.io signed-release endpoint; any runtime code changes beyond what the install-model decision strictly requires.

## Acceptance criteria

- Packaging-mechanics scoping doc exists and answers bundle format, versioning, sync/cron-on-install, and profile.toml defaults with concrete decisions.
- A recorded decision on install model (shim vs binary) with the stub either scheduled or explicitly deferred with rationale.
- Marketplace submission checklist reviewed against actual Hermes plugin catalog requirements.
- Compat matrix defining supported runtime version ranges and how violations surface at install time.
- ag-infra-cdp can proceed using only artifacts from this epic.

## Open questions

- M6 (hermes env-backend filesystem view) is unresolved: does it affect marketplace installs, or only the ACP walk harness? Contingency: ship with library-channel delivery (per the research doc's "deliver the guide via hermes's library channel and make walk_read_step library-aware") and document the limitation.
- Does the Hermes marketplace require a pinned runtime version, or can the shim model's PATH detection suffice? Contingency: pin via `uv tool install agentguides==X.Y.*` in the install hook.
- Where does the signed-release endpoint live if Model A is ever needed (agentguides.io vs GitHub releases)?
